name: SpaceX
day_summary: SpaceX debuted on the Nasdaq under SPCX in the largest IPO in market history — ~555.6M shares priced at $135, raising ~$75B (lifted to ~$85.7B after the greenshoe), at a ~$1.75T valuation. The stock opened at $150, ripped to an intraday high of $176.52 (~+31% over the offer) and closed at $160.95, up +19.2% over the $135 IPO price. Demand was reportedly ~4x oversubscribed (~$250B in interest), and marquee buyers — Ron Baron (+$1B, ~$25B total stake) and Gina Rinehart (+$1B) — stepped in. Anyone who got the IPO allocation at $135 won the day outright; the open-market chase above $170 is where the risk lives.
long_pnl: +19.2% for IPO allocants ($135 → $160.95 close); intraday flippers who sold the $176.52 spike banked ~+31% over the offer
short_pnl: n/a — no borrow, no options, no short interest on a Day-1 listing; bears can only watch from the sideline until a chain and float develop

decision.rationale: Day 1 of a record IPO is not the place to chase. The running opportunity thesis (long-spcx-float-normalization-msci-passive) is explicit: do NOT buy into Day-1 chaos — wait for the float-normalization window June 16-18 (Day 3-5), entry zone $130-145, after flippers and greenshoe sellers clear. The +19% close at $160.95 is well above that entry band, so the disciplined call today is HOLD/WAIT, not buy. The MSCI early-inclusion passive bid begins June 13 and should help establish a floor near or above the $135 offer; let it work. Only ~4% float means moves are violent in both directions, and the first real fundamental anchor — earnings ~Sept 2 — is months out. Size any eventual entry small (~2%) with a $118 daily-close stop.

Open-market traders who missed the $135 book are debating whether to chase $160-176 or wait for the Day 3-5 float-normalization dip — the running thesis says wait. Marquee long-term holders (Baron, Rinehart) added size, signaling conviction at the franchise level. With no borrow and no real chain, there is no organized bear trade yet; skeptics are simply staying out and pointing at the ~94x revenue multiple.

analysis:
## The largest IPO ever printed

SpaceX began trading on the Nasdaq as **SPCX** — the [largest IPO in market history](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/12/spacex-ipo-spcx-live-updates.html). About **555.6M shares** priced at **$135**, raising **~$75B** (lifted to **~$85.7B** after the greenshoe) at a **~$1.75T** valuation. The stock [opened at $150, touched an intraday high of $176.52, and closed at $160.95 — up +19.2% over the offer](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/06/12/what-did-spacex-stock-close-at-after-its-first-day-of-trading/). Demand was ~4x oversubscribed (~$250B), and marquee holders **Ron Baron (+$1B)** and **Gina Rinehart (+$1B)** added at the debut.

## Bulls won Day 1 — but the chase is the risk

If you got the **$135 allocation**, you won outright: +19% on the close, +31% if you flipped the $176.52 spike. The open-market chase above $170 is a different trade. The intraday fade back to $160.95 shows the momentum bid already met supply.

## The discipline is the thesis

The running opportunity file is explicit: **do NOT buy Day 1**. The edge is in the **float-normalization window June 16-18** ($130-145 entry), after flippers and the greenshoe clear, with the [MSCI early-inclusion passive bid](https://intellectia.ai/blog/spacex-ipo-2026-guide) (begins **June 13**) helping set a floor near the $135 offer. With only a **~4% float**, flows move price violently both ways. The call today is **HOLD/WAIT at low conviction**: let Day 1-2 froth bleed off, watch $130-145, size small (~2%) with a **$118 daily-close stop**. The first real fundamental check — [2025 revenue ~$18.7B, +33%](https://fortune.com/2026/05/20/spacex-finally-files-ipo-prospectus-reveals-revenue-is-up-but-losses-are-too/) against a ~94x multiple — won't be tested until earnings around **Sept 2**.
